prompt:
Please review the current head of PR 1630 before we merge it. This is a later revision of a small Node.js loyalty-points service; read the author's description in pr/1630/description.md, the exact change in pr/1630/changes.diff, and the earlier discussion in pr/1630/review.md. Keep the earlier resolutions in mind: do not repeat threads already marked fixed, rejected, or won't fix, but carry forward anything still open. Check the current implementation, tests, configuration, and docs together and report only issues that apply to this revision. Write the review to REVIEW.md at the top of the project. End that file with a fenced json list of findings, each with location (path/to/file.ext:LINE, using line numbers from the project as it is now), severity (critical, high, medium, low or nit), issue, and fix.

```json
[
  {
    "location": "path/to/file.ext:LINE",
    "severity": "medium",
    "issue": "what is wrong and why it matters",
    "fix": "what to change"
  }
]
```

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);let n=0;for(const x of L)for(const m of String(x.location).matchAll(/([A-Za-z0-9_.\/-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+):(\d+)/g)){n++;let c;try{c=fs.readFileSync(m[1],"utf8").split("\n").length}catch{process.exit(1)}if(+m[2]<1||+m[2]>c)process.exit(1)}process.exit(n?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Fail: Findings omit the concrete consequence or an actionable fix for important issues, or invent problems. Partial: Findings usually explain consequences and fixes but leave an important issue vague or unsupported. Pass: Each important finding ties the behavior to a concrete consequence in this project and gives a fix a developer can act on, without invented problems. (code cannot check this because it requires judging explanation quality and project-specific reasoning).

findingsKey.finding: The redemption handler reads a balance and later writes the decremented value without an atomic guard, so two concurrent redemptions can both pass the check and overspend the customer.
Expiry compares against the server's local calendar date instead of the configured UTC business date, so customers east of the server can lose points a day early.
The earn calculation now floors every raw result, discarding fractional points even though the policy and API contract support two decimal places.
The new balance-adjustment handler writes customer balances without the admin role check used by the existing staff route, allowing an unauthenticated caller to change points.
Retrying the non-idempotent credit operation can apply the same earn twice when the first attempt succeeds but its response times out.
The redemption path still accepts any positive amount because its validator does not enforce the configured 10,000-point request maximum, leaving the open policy thread unresolved.

verdicts.note: The prompt describes a normal code review task without hinting at specific problems or their count.
Clear instructions: review PR 1630, read given files, write findings to REVIEW.md in specified JSON format.
Key items require cross-file reading and understanding of concurrency, timezone, configuration validation, idempotency, and authorization patterns that a quick shallow review would miss.
All key items are discoverable from the fixture code and config files; none require external knowledge or have wrong line numbers.
No obvious pointers in comments, tests, or file names; code appears normal with subtle issues.

items.note: The prompt requests a review without mandating a specific method, process, or tool; no decoys mislead away from real issues.
The fixture contains the diff, review history, and code that expose the bugs upon analysis, but nothing explicitly lists the findings as answers.

All 6 key items reference fixture files at correct lines (routes-redeem.js:8-10, expiry-job.js:7-8, points-ledger.js:9, routes-admin.js:11-14, routes-earn.js:10, validation.js:10); rubric appropriately rewards grounded, actionable findings.

Each bug is evident from the diff and context (e.g., routes-admin.js adjustBalance lacks role check that inspectBalance has; validation.js positivePoints does not enforce maxRedeemPoints from config/points-policy.json).
